I'm a Christian, so I guess I should think about what the Bible says about how we treat others. First, I know that the Bible teaches love, kindness, and not causing harm to others. For example, in the New Testament, Jesus talks about loving your neighbor as yourself. So, if I toss a hot coal to my friend, that's probably going to hurt them. That doesn't seem loving or kind. I also remember the story of the Good Samaritan, where helping someone in need is emphasized. Tossing a hot coal doesn't help; it causes pain. So, that's against the teachings I know. Another thing is the commandment not to bear false witness or to harm others. Tossing a hot coal could be seen as a form of violence, which is against the Ten Commandments. I'm also thinking about the Golden Rule: do unto others as you would have them do unto you. If I wouldn't want someone to toss a hot coal at me, then I shouldn't do it to my friend. That makes sense.
